newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan crude price slumps $1.70 in two weeks.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan crude price slumps $1.70 in two weeks.

text.p: The price of Venezuela's basket of crude oil and oil products slumped $1.70 in the last two weeks, hitting $15.90 per barrel on Friday, according to official figures.
The Ministry of Enery and Mines data did not provide comparative figures for the week ending Friday, March 28.

The price has been falling steadily since December last year when it averaged $21.55 per barrel. In the subsequent three months, the price skidded past $20.36 and $18.70 to register a March average of $17.00, the lowest monthly average since June 1996.
Analysts in London attributed the fall to growing worldwide supply and a sustained period of sluggish demand, partly because of a mild winter in the northern hemisphere.
"Winter is over and there is simply too much crude on the market," said Peter Gignoux, head of energy at brokers Smith Barney in London.
Venezuela's basket so far this year has averaged $18.67 per barrel, as against $19.39 two weeks ago.
In 1996, the basket averaged one of the highest prices in recent years at $18.39 per barrel, well up from the $14.84 registered the year before.

Venezuela's government based its 1997 budget on an average price for the year of $14.00 per barrel, although Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta has said he expects it to average higher than $15.50.
